original.prompt: Consider the following statements about digital payment fees in India, as of August 2026:
items: The Merchant Discount Rate is a processing fee that merchants pay to banks and payment service providers.
UPI has been free of merchant fees since 2019.
Regulations cap the Merchant Discount Rate on debit cards at a maximum of 3%.
original.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: Debit card fees are capped by regulation at 0.9%. The 3% figure is the level that credit card MDR can reach. UPI's fee-free status since 2019 helped it process transactions worth INR 30 trillion in July 2026.
original.source: whereas debit card fees are capped by regulations at a maximum of 0.9%

rewritten.prompt: Consider the following statements about digital payment fees in India, as of August 2026:
items: The Merchant Discount Rate is a processing fee that merchants pay to banks and payment service providers.
UPI has been free of merchant fees since 2019.
Regulations cap the Merchant Discount Rate on debit cards at a maximum of 0.9%.
rewritten.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
rewritten.explain: All three statements are correct: MDR is a fee merchants pay to banks and payment service providers, UPI has been free of merchant fees since 2019, and debit card fees are capped by regulation at 0.9%. By contrast, credit card MDR can reach as high as 3%, and officials are weighing a 0.3% to 0.5% MDR on UPI transactions above INR 2,000.
rewritten.source: In contrast, credit card MDR can reach as high as 3%, whereas debit card fees are capped by regulations at a maximum of 0.9%.
